note: Mexican Spanish: what differs from Spanish elsewhere, as data (review 3.2). The reader understands every variety's words at once; answers and the voice use the city's variety. 19 Nov 2026.

orita.means: ahorita, as speech to text often writes it

almuerzo.means: a late breakfast, around 10:00–12:00 (in Spain: lunch)

comida.means: the main midday meal, around 14:00–17:00 (also: food)

antojitos.means: street snacks: sopes, gorditas, tlayudas, quesadillas

clock.para: cuarto para las nueve = 8:45; diez para las nueve = 8:50 (Mexico)
clock.menos: las nueve menos cuarto = 8:45 (Spain; understood here too)

voice.seseo: c before e/i and z sound as s (no θ)
voice.yeismo: ll and y sound the same (ʝ)
voice.jota: j, and g before e/i: a soft x or h, not Spain's χ
voice.x: México, Oaxaca, Xalapa: x as j; Xola, Xocolatl and many Nahuatl names: x as sh; Xochimilco: x as s. Rules cannot choose: the city pack carries the reading
voice.unstressedVowels: central Mexico often shortens or drops unstressed vowels in fast speech (pues → ps): a recognizer must expect it
